message.content: Nicolaus Copernicus developed his heliocentric theory during the early sixteenth century, a period of profound European transformation. The Renaissance challenged medieval scholasticism while the Catholic Church maintained immense political and intellectual authority over the continent. In Poland, where Copernicus served as a canon in Frombork, relative stability under the Jagiellonian dynasty contrasted with the fractured politics of the Holy Roman Empire. His models, though cactiform in their earliest scribbled notes, represented a revolutionary break from geocentric orthodoxy. The Reformation, beginning in 1517, further destabilized religious authority and created space for new cosmic ideas.
